I have been farming these 10 mu for 30 years, and my mother farmed here before me. I went to primary school, then came back to the fields. I know this land.

Last year my wheat did about 500 jin per mu, and the maize did a bit better, around 600 jin. This year I will do more or less the same, maybe push the fertilizer a little because the wheat price is up and I want to make sure I don't lose yield. My son works in the county town, so it's mostly me and my husband in the fields, though we hire two people for a few days at harvest if we need to.

**Wheat**  
I plant wheat in the autumn, right after the National Day holiday. I use the improved seed that the dealer in town sells — I think it's called Jimai something, the one with the red bag. Last year I used 25 jin of seed per mu, so about 12.5 kg. This year I will do the same. I spread compound fertilizer as base — I buy the 15-15-15 bag, about 50 kg per mu as base, then top-dress with urea in the spring when the wheat turns green. For the top-dressing I put another 15 kg of urea per mu. So total nitrogen is maybe around 18 kg per mu if I count it all, phosphorus around 7–8 kg, potassium about 7–8 kg. I irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray fungicide and insecticide twice — once in spring and once if I see aphids. I till with the rotary tiller before planting.

**Maize**  
After we harvest wheat in early June, I plant maize right away. I use hybrid seed, the yellow bag from the same dealer. I plant about 2.5 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, then top-dress with urea at the big-flare stage, about 15 kg per mu. So nitrogen ends up around 16–17 kg per mu, phosphorus around 6 kg, potassium around 6 kg. Maize needs less irrigation here because summer rain usually helps, but last few years the rain has been strange, so I irrigate twice — once at jointing if it's dry, and once at filling. I spray pesticide twice, mainly for armyworm and the stem borers. I don't till again for maize, just plant directly after wheat harvest with the no-till planter, or sometimes I do a quick rotary till if the stubble is too thick.

Costs worry me. A 50 kg bag of compound is over 150 yuan now, and urea went up too. But if I cut back and the yield drops, I lose more than I save. So I keep the same as last year. My neighbor with the 8 mu plot uses about the same amounts, and he had good maize last year, so I copy him.
